design.title: Cross-survey blending: every training view becomes a per-pixel mixture of the three surveys' photographs of the same place, so the model learns the continuum between surveys instead of three fingerprints
design.eli5: The model has seen Berlin in three different aerial photographs: one in summer, one in winter with bare trees, one in early spring. So far it could pass its training by learning each photograph by heart - three separate memories of every street - and a brand-new fourth photograph matched none of them. We now show it, while it learns, pictures that are blends of the three: half summer and half winter, or winter on the left side of the frame and spring on the right. In a blend, no single photograph's look can be trusted, but the shapes of the roads, blocks and canals are the same in all three and come through sharp every time. The hope is that the model is pushed to remember the city by its shape, and that a photograph it has never seen then looks like just another blend.
design.hypothesis: Four results in this era, read together, say the held-out survey fails for a reason no experiment has yet addressed: the model has exactly three appearance samples per place and nothing in training says what lies BETWEEN them. (1) Experiment 5 showed the gap is survey, not viewpoint: with a whole-frame trunk the three TRAINING photographs reached 72-81% usable at the same 11-17 m off-lattice eval viewpoints (train_capture_diagnostics 0.335 / 0.258 / 0.238) while the held-out 2024 photograph of the same viewpoints stayed at 12.5% usable / 42.3% false fix (1.298). (2) Experiment 3 showed that forcing the three surveys' features to AGREE does not transfer: its logged final cross-survey cosine was 0.935 (train_berlin.log, consistency loss 0.065), i.e. the three training appearances of each place were mapped to nearly the same 160-d vector, and 2024 got WORSE (false fix 65.3% -> 71.8%, 1.583 -> 1.648). Agreement on three points constrains two directions of appearance space per place; a fourth survey lands somewhere else. (3) Experiment 4's photometric randomisation (kept, 1.583 -> 1.271) covers the GLOBAL part of a survey change - exposure, colour pipeline, sharpness - and cannot synthesise the CONTENT part: leaf-on vs leaf-off canopy, shadow direction and length, parked cars, construction, the leaning roofs of a standard DOP vs a true-ortho. (4) A model-free design-time probe on the three TRAINING captures only (runs/_probe_exp6_scale.py; the eval capture was never opened): over 600 random lattice places, nearest-neighbour retrieval by per-crop standardised pixel correlation identifies a place across surveys from the SAME pixel-aligned viewpoint 90-97% of the time at 1 m/px (mean same-place correlation 0.49-0.57), rising only to 0.60-0.65 at 8-16 m/px - so (a) pixel-aligned surveys share most of their structure and a representation that locates one from another is not asking the impossible, (b) the survey difference is broadband, not fine texture, so a coarse-scale bottleneck is NOT the lever (that candidate was considered and dropped on this measurement), and (c) the same probe collapses to 7-11% under a 12 px shift and 1% under shift+rotation, confirming that viewpoint tolerance is the CNN's learned contribution and must be learned jointly with survey tolerance, not bolted on at decode. What the training signal lacks is DENSITY along the survey axis. The captures are pixel-aligned on one grid (alignment <= 1 px) and extract_chunk already pulls each position from all three captures under one shared heading, so a convex per-pixel combination of the three crops is a physically meaningful synthetic photograph of the same place: half summer canopy and half leaf-off, a shadow at an intermediate strength, a car at half opacity. With a SPATIALLY VARYING weight field, one frame holds a leafy tree beside a bare one, east shadows beside west shadows - states no real survey contains - so canopy, shadow, movable objects and colour pipeline become locally uninformative, while road, block, building-footprint and water geometry, which every blend renders crisply because it is identical in all three sources, stays the only cue that always pays. This is mixup/CutMix applied along the survey axis of aligned imagery; it is possible only because of this era's data asset (every earlier era had one photograph, and no row in lineage_history mentions mixing or blending across photographs), and it is a materially different angle from experiment 3: instead of asking the features of three fixed points to agree, it asks the classifier to be correct on the whole simplex between them, which is where a fourth survey is far more likely to fall than on any one of the three vertices. Capacity spent on three pixel-exact fingerprints per cell is capacity the blend augmentation makes worthless; capacity spent on shared geometry is rewarded on every blend and - the bet - on truedop_2024.
